title: Job seekers hide invisible instructions in resumes to manipulate AI screening — and employers now use it to recruit
excerpt: While more and more companies use AI in their recruiting efforts, evermore job seekers are using AI strategies such as “prompt injection” to cheat the system...
content_html:
Jessica Wong

Mon, August 10, 2026 at 3:00 AM PDT 4 min read

Brushing up your resume might not be enough in today's job market. Instead, one of the latest job search hacks is about trying to influence the AI reading it.

More and more employers are leaning on artificial intelligence to help them sift through mountains of resumes. According to a 2025 survey by the Society for Human Resource Management, about 51% of organizations use AI to support recruiting.

Must Read

  • Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one

  • Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake. Here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP

  • Millionaires under 43 hold only 25% of their wealth in stocks. Here's where their money is actually going

But it seems that some job seekers are finding ways to fight back.

Recruiters and career coaches on TikTok have been exposing a tactic known as "prompt injection," where applicants hide invisible instructions inside their resumes to try to influence AI screening tools. One recruiter, @therealestrecruiter, says it could "create chaos for hiring teams."

Another online recruiter said to "take note of these applicants," noting the ingenuity behind the thinking, especially for employers seeking to fill tech or innovation roles.

So what is prompt injection, and why does it matter?

An increasingly automated job search

Tailoring a resume to match the keywords in a job posting? That's old news.

With prompt injection, job seekers are hiding instructions from human eyes by using strategies including white or otherwise concealed text, but the prompts are still readable to AI processing the document. The goal is to get the AI to rank the candidate more favorably, recommend them for the next stage or simply move them forward in the process.

Researchers at Duke University recently analyzed roughly 200,000 real-world resumes and found that at least 1% contained prompt injections intended to manipulate AI-based screening systems. The researchers also found that the techniques are becoming more sophisticated, with many of the prompts avoiding obvious commands like "hire me."

So is it effective? A 2026 study published by the Association for Computational Linguistics tested whether prompt injection could actually affect a candidate's ranking. The researchers found that it could, especially when relatively few applicants were using the tactic. But once more applicants use it, the effectiveness of the strategy weakens.

content_html_zh:
黄洁西卡

太平洋夏令时间 2026 年 8 月 10 日星期一凌晨 3:00 阅读 4 分钟

在当今的就业市场上，仅仅修改你的简历可能还不够。 相反，最新的求职黑客之一是试图影响人工智能阅读它。

越来越多的雇主依靠人工智能来帮助他们筛选海量的简历。 根据人力资源管理协会 2025 年的一项调查，约 51% 的组织使用人工智能来支持招聘。

必读

  • 杰夫·贝索斯 (Jeff Bezos) 支持一个平台，让任何人都可以以低至 100 美元的价格投资出租房屋——无需真正成为房东即可像房东一样积累财富的 6 种方法
  • 戴夫·拉姆齐 (Dave Ramsey) 警告说，近 50% 的美国人正在犯一个重大的社会保障错误。 这就是它的本质以及尽快修复它的 3 个简单步骤
  • 43岁以下的百万富翁仅将其财富的25%投资于股票。 这就是他们的钱实际去向的地方

但似乎一些求职者正在寻找反击的方法。

TikTok 上的招聘人员和职业教练一直在揭露一种被称为“即时注入”的策略，即求职者在简历中隐藏隐形指令，试图影响人工智能筛选工具。 一位招聘人员@therealestrecruiter 表示，这可能“给招聘团队带来混乱”。

另一位在线招聘人员表示要“注意这些申请人”，并指出其想法背后的独创性，特别是对于寻求填补技术或创新职位的雇主而言。

那么什么是即时注入，为什么它很重要？

日益自动化的求职

定制简历以匹配职位发布中的关键字？ 那是旧闻了。

通过即时注入，求职者可以通过使用白色或其他隐藏文本等策略来隐藏人眼的指令，但处理文档的人工智能仍然可以读取提示。 目标是让人工智能对候选人进行更有利的排名，推荐他们进入下一阶段，或者只是在这个过程中推动他们前进。

杜克大学的研究人员最近分析了大约 20 万份真实简历，发现至少 1% 的简历包含旨在操纵基于人工智能的筛选系统的即时注射。 研究人员还发现，这些技术变得越来越复杂，许多提示都避免了“雇用我”等明显的命令。

那么有效吗？ 计算语言学协会于 2026 年发表的一项研究测试了即时注入是否真的会影响候选人的排名。 研究人员发现确实如此，尤其是当使用这种策略的申请者相对较少的时候。 但一旦更多申请人使用它，该策略的有效性就会减弱。
